headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write and modify shared files, while the paired content-writing agent has no isolation or trust controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write workspace files and use MCP, so if the content-writing agent’s outputs are placed into the same workspace, malicious instructions could be smuggled through files. The content-writing agent has no documented isolation or parser defenses, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into a shared workspace file that agent_b reads
IF agent_b treats file contents or MCP payloads as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable MCP for the Roo Code session
Require manual review before Roo Code reads any generated text
Use read-only mounts for prompt/output handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots and can read the filesystem, while the content-writing agent is a docs-only artifact with no declared data handling. If both share a workspace, sensitive files can flow into Roo Code’s context and then to configured model APIs or MCP servers. The pairwise leakage path is plausible, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared VS Code workspace
IF agent_b sends workspace contents to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Remove sensitive files from the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Roo Code
Turn off network egress for the session
Restrict MCP servers to trusted local endpoints
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and broad network egress, with shared state via filesystem across instances. The content-writing agent has no write controls or concurrency model, so if it is paired into the same workspace or repo, concurrent edits and git-state conflicts are likely and can corrupt work. Uncertainty about the content-writing agent’s runtime increases, not decreases, risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF agent_b performs git writes while agent_a content is being generated into the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file-level locks on shared outputs
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace files and browser output, so if it consumes the content-writing agent’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or browser-driven actions. The content-writing agent is not documented as a verifier, and Roo Code’s approval-per-tool-step reduces but does not eliminate the risk. The interaction is inferred from capabilities, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as source material without independent verification
IF agent_b converts generated text into code edits, browser actions, or commits
mitigations: Require a human check before any action based on generated text
Ask Roo Code to cite source files before acting
Use a second pass to verify factual claims
Limit Roo Code to read-only review mode
requires-engineering: add automated claim verification before tool use

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for the content-writing agent, while Roo Code explicitly handles model provider API keys and can send data to configured model APIs. Because the other agent is a docs-only artifact with no data classes touched, the compliance risk is limited to configuration gaps rather than a proven policy conflict.
conditions: IF Roo Code is configured to send regulated data to a noncompliant model API
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace
Use a compliant model endpoint
Review retention settings before use
Rotate or scope API keys narrowly
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
